feedback.description: BR-11 (an employee's upskilling plan MUST contain at least 2-3 catalog items, of which at least one is AI-enabled) is a stated, enforceable business rule that the §8 compliance success metric ('Live % vs the 2-3/year target') depends on — yet NO acceptance criterion validates it. 'AI-enabled' appears in the AC set only inside AC-09 (catalog tagging), never as a plan-selection constraint. The acceptance-criteria coverage_matrix has no row for BR-11. With no pass/fail gate, plan-minimum enforcement and the compliance % computation will be built inconsistently or omitted.
feedback.suggestion: Add a P1 AC (e.g. AC-26) with GIVEN an employee assembling their yearly plan / WHEN they attempt to finalize a plan with fewer than 2 items OR zero AI-enabled items / THEN the plan is rejected with a specific user-facing message and is NOT marked complete; and GIVEN a plan with >=2 items including >=1 AI-enabled / THEN it is accepted and counts toward the compliance metric. Add a coverage_matrix row mapping BR-11 -> the new AC.

feedback.description: UC-1 lists the action 'select >=2-3 items (must include >=1 AI-enabled)' but no user journey covers the boundary/error behavior of the plan-selection constraint: what the user SEES when they try to finalize a non-conforming plan (too few items or no AI-enabled item), and whether items can be removed/swapped after selection. The empty-state references the requirement narratively but the enforcement flow and its error message are undefined (silence = undefined behavior). This is the flow-level counterpart to PRD-R2-001 (the missing AC).
feedback.suggestion: In UC-1 (or a short dedicated journey) document the plan-validation flow: the explicit rule (>=2-3 items, >=1 AI-enabled), the user-facing message on a non-conforming attempt, and the remove/replace-an-item path. Mirror it in the §10 Error Handling table (Flow: Plan selection / Invalid input: <2 items or 0 AI-enabled / User sees: <message>).

feedback.description: The optional manager 'endorsed' catalog flag is listed as in-scope (PRD UC-5 'Manager may set an endorsed flag'; scope-boundary In-Scope 'optional manager endorsed flag') but has no validating AC, so its behavior (who may set it, what it affects in matching/recommendations) is untested and ambiguous. Minor tension with scope-boundary line 79, which lists 'endorsement workflows' as a creep risk — the single flag is in-scope while workflows around it are out; the distinction is coherent but the flag's exact, testable behavior is unspecified.
feedback.suggestion: Either add a brief P2 AC for the endorsed flag (GIVEN a manager / WHEN they toggle 'endorsed' on a catalog item / THEN the item is marked endorsed and a non-manager cannot set it), or explicitly demote it to a clearly labeled nice-to-have / drop it to remove the loose end. Reaffirm in scope that only the flag (not any workflow) is in-scope.
